history.summary: The Somnath Mahadev Temple stands in Saurath village, Madhubani district (CSV town 'Madhubani' corrected to Saurath), a village famed for the Saurath Sabha, the centuries-old Maithil Brahmin marriage-assembly fair. Per enduring local folklore, when the Somnath temple at Saurashtra (Gujarat) was raided by Mahmud of Ghazni, priests hailing from Saurath returned to their native village and founded this temple, naming it Somnath — 'Saurath' itself is said to derive from 'Saurashtra' (folk claim, UNVERIFIED). The temple is centuries old but its founding date is undocumented. In 2026, Bihar's Tourism Minister Arun Shankar Prasad visited the site and pledged full government support for its conservation and development.

name: Somnath Mahadev Temple, Saurath
town_description: Saurath is a village in Madhubani district in the Mithila region of northern Bihar, about 10 km from Madhubani town. It is best known for the Saurath Sabha, a historic annual gathering (under a banyan grove, Sabha Gachhi) where Maithil families traditionally arranged marriages. The village hosts the ancient Somnath Mahadev temple and sits in the heart of the Madhubani-painting cultural belt.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Mahashivratri and Shravan month for the spiritual peak
